facts.fact: Vermont is the largest producer of maple syrup in the United States; sap is collected in buckets hung on taps (spiles) in sugar maples in late winter.
A Donald Ross course (1924), restored by Dr. Michael Hurdzan (1998), beside the University of Vermont.
The course is tree-lined by northern hardwoods with white pine and hemlock (the lidar finds mostly broadleaf crowns).

concepts.name: Sugaring Season
concepts.rationale: A galvanised sap bucket hung on a sugar maple's spile, heaped with golf balls instead of sap, and a scarlet maple leaf: Vermont's sugarbush and the course's hardwoods, with a golfer's wink.
concepts.symbolism: The bucket is Vermont; the balls in place of sap are the game.
concepts.interpretation: The golf balls in the bucket are a joke, not history.
concepts.strengths: Reads at 32 px as a bucket of balls; says Vermont without words; no other course uses the subject.
concepts.tradeoffs: Says Vermont more than Burlington (Lake Champlain's 'Champ' was the other idea; it is close to a local team's mascot, so not drawn).
